title: temperature
description: v0.1 device-model entity: a standalone temperature sensor (1-Wire DS18B20 probe or the Pi's own CPU thermal zone) read directly by the renewvan/node-temperature node (sensing, not a feed remap). Published under renewvan/temperature/<id>/<property>, where <id> is the user-assigned sensor id from config.ini (or the probe's serial when unconfigured). temperature_c is ALWAYS degrees Celsius on the wire; 'unit' is a display preference only -- consumers convert for rendering. Identity fields (name, unit, source, serial) are retained and published once at startup and again whenever a user edit lands on the <field>/set command topic; live fields (temperature_c, status) are republished every poll (default 3s). Sensors that sit on another entity's hardware (tank water temperature, battery temperature) stay on that entity's own temperature_c field and are not duplicated here.

name.description: Human-readable label shown on the dashboard (e.g. 'Fridge'). User-editable via renewvan/temperature/<id>/name/set; persisted by the node and overrides the config.ini default. Identity field.

unit.description: Display unit preference for this sensor. Does NOT change the unit of temperature_c (always Celsius). User-editable via renewvan/temperature/<id>/unit/set; persisted by the node and overrides the config.ini default. Identity field.

source.description: Where the reading comes from: 'w1' = 1-Wire DS18B20 probe, 'cpu' = Raspberry Pi SoC thermal zone. Identity field.

serial.description: 1-Wire device id (e.g. '28-0000075a1b2c'), the stable hardware identity of the probe. Present only when source is 'w1'. Identity field.

temperature_c.description: Temperature in degrees Celsius. Only republished while status is 'ok'; when status is not 'ok' the node skips the publish (same as node-tank's NTC failure behavior) and the LAST retained value stays on the broker, so consumers MUST gate on status == 'ok' before rendering it. Range is the DS18B20 operating range (-55..125) widened to cover the Pi SoC. Live field.

status.description: Sensor health. 'ok' = fresh valid reading; 'no_reading' = the sensor is present but the read failed or was out of range (CRC failure, 85.0 C power-on default, unparseable file); 'disconnected' = a previously-seen 1-Wire probe has vanished from the bus. Live field.
